newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISA WANTS OTC SHARES ON MAIN MARKET.
newsitem.headline: POLISA WANTS OTC SHARES ON MAIN MARKET.

text.p: Polish insurer Polisa SA applied to the bourse on Thursday to transfer its 4.27 million shares now traded on the regulated over-the-counter market to the bourse's main floor, the company's deputy president said.

"Interest in the OTC market has been shrinking and shares have low liquidity there. We want their owners to have the same access to bourse trade as other shareholders do," Zygfryd Kielarski told Reuters.

Polisa entered the OTC market, or Centrala Tabela Ofert (CTO), in mid-December because it wanted its shareholders to get tax breaks on capital gains granted on shares which were publicly floated but acquired before the firm became public.
Polisa currently has 4.1 million shares traded on the main market of the Warsaw bourse.
